prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1394; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a low-speed head-on collision on a two-lane road. Insured reports the other vehicle crossed the center line during a slight curve. Both vehicles drivable from scene. Insured states no airbag deployment. Police report requested.

Entry 2: Claimant contacted our office through counsel, who confirmed representation and requested that all further communication be directed to his firm. Claimant reports a wrist injury treated at urgent care and a referral for orthopedic follow-up. Medical authorization requested through counsel.

Entry 3: Police report received. Responding officer noted minor front-end damage to both vehicles and assigned fault to the other driver for crossing the center line. Witness statement from a passenger in the insured vehicle is consistent with the insured's account. Liability appears clear, pending review.

Entry 4: Counsel's office provided imaging results confirming a distal radius fracture and a treatment plan that includes a cast and possible physical therapy. Demand package expected once treatment concludes. Reserve reviewed and adjusted to reflect the bodily injury exposure. Referred to the bodily injury unit for handling.

Entry 5: Vehicle inspection completed. Repair estimate reviewed and approved for the front bumper, hood, and headlamp assembly. Supervisor notified of the represented bodily injury component. Next step is to await the medical records and the formal demand from counsel before evaluating settlement.
